analysis.evidence: וּזֲהַב הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא means “and the gold of that land.” The construct זֲהַב takes הָאָרֶץ as its complement, and טוֹב describes the gold as good.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed conjunction וּ־.

analysis.evidence: וּזֲהַב הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא means “and the gold of that land.” The demonstrative identifies a particular territory, and שָׁם (“there”) locates the other materials in it.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, with feminine agreement.

analysis.evidence: In הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא, “that land,” הַהִוא follows הָאָרֶץ and agrees with it in gender, number, and definiteness. The Pentateuchal spelling הוא is pointed הִוא for the feminine pronoun הִיא.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ + third-person feminine singular pronoun, used demonstratively.

analysis.evidence: In וּזֲהַב הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא טוֹב, “the gold of that land is good,” טוֹב agrees with the masculine singular זֲהַב and describes the quality of the gold.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective, used predicatively.
analysis.sense: good in quality, fine, fit for use

analysis.evidence: שָׁם points back to הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא, “that land,” and indicates where the bdellium and the onyx stone are found.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add בְּדֹלַח under its own consonants בדלח. Neither passage establishes a derivation from the verb בָּדַל.
draft.definition: A material found in Havilah, traditionally called bdellium.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:12 lists it among Havilah’s resources. Numbers 11:7 compares the appearance of manna to it.

analysis.evidence: After mentioning the land’s gold, Genesis 2:12 uses שָׁם (‘there’) to locate both הַבְּדֹלַח and the שֹׁהַם stone in Havilah. The list identifies בְּדֹלַח as a material found there but leaves its composition uncertain.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: a material from the land of Havilah, traditionally identified as bdellium

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶבֶן הַשֹּׁהַם ‘and the onyx stone’, אֶבֶן names the gem and הַשֹּׁהַם specifies its kind. The conjunction links it to הַבְּדֹלַח ‘the bdellium’ as another material found there.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular construct, prefixed with the conjunction וְ ‘and’.

draft.change: Create a lexical article for the stone noun שֹׁהַם under its own consonants שהמ.
draft.definition: A precious stone traditionally identified as onyx.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:12 explicitly calls it a stone. Exodus 28:9–12 describes two such stones engraved with names and set in gold on the shoulders of the ephod.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶבֶן הַשֹּׁהַם, “and the onyx stone,” שֹׁהַם specifies the kind of אֶבֶן. The verse lists it alongside gold and bdellium among the materials found in the land. The wording establishes that it is a stone, though its exact mineral identity is uncertain.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun with prefixed definite article הַ־, which doubles the initial שׁ.
analysis.sense: A precious stone traditionally identified as onyx.
